text:
marta: heads-up — saw duplicate job runs when our async client retried after a 503. idempotency header wasn't preserved.
marta: repro summary: POST /v1/launch with header 'Idempotency-Key' -> transient 503 -> retry -> second request lacks header -> server creates another launch.
liam: can you drop the minimal snippet?
marta: async example: 
```python
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(key=REDWOOD_KEY) as client:
    await client.post('/v1/launch', json=payload, headers={'Idempotency-Key': run_id})
```
marta: stackwise it looks like our async retry path reconstructs a new aiohttp request without copying custom headers (session default auth exists so Authorization shows up, but not user headers).
sven: thanks. sounds like our RetryState only keeps method/url/body/timeout and loses headers. That's dangerous for idempotent POSTs.
ciara: proposed fix: store a small header map on the RetryContext but only persist a safe list (e.g., Idempotency-Key, X-Request-ID). Make the header whitelist configurable at client init.
liam: agree. API suggestion: RedwoodAsyncClient(..., replay_preserve_headers=['Idempotency-Key']). Default should include 'Idempotency-Key' so existing users don't see regressions.
sven: we should be explicit in docs about replay semantics and warn about replaying ephemeral cookies. Also ensure Authorization is only replayed if using SDK-managed auth (we sign it internally).
ciara: add types: RetryContext.preserved_headers: Optional[Dict[str,str]] and client param typing as Sequence[str]. That helps mypy and prevents accidental unions.
marta: tests I'll add: unit test that simulates ServerDisconnectedError/503 and asserts the second HTTP call contains same Idempotency-Key; integration test hitting /staging/launch to ensure only one resource created on retries.
liam: also tweak retry classification for transient errors: treat 502/503/504 + connection resets as retryable; avoid replay on 4xx except 429 maybe.
sven: and add randomized jitter to exponential backoff to reduce thundering herd. default backoff: base=0.5, factor=2, jitter=0.2.
ciara: small UX ask: can we expose a helper on the client to build idempotent POSTs? e.g., client.post_idempotent(path, json=..., idempotency_key=...). That would auto-wire the header and be less error-prone.
marta: good idea — I can include that in the PR as sugar.
deploy-bot: created_issue GH#4899 — "python-async: preserve idempotency and configurable replay headers for retries" assigned to @marta.
liam: changelog note: BREAKING? not really but behavioral change. We should document default preserved header and migration steps. Ops teams may have relied on 'no-preserve' behavior.
sven: we'll also add an integration smoke to our e2e suite that verifies no duplicate resources when simulating transient 5xxs.
ciara: perf note — lowering default async socket timeout to 15s prevents long-hanging requests that cause cascading retries in low-bandwidth environments. Mention in docs.
marta: PR will add: 1) replay_preserve_headers param, 2) store headers in RetryContext, 3) ensure _rebuild_request merges preserved headers (client headers take precedence over session), 4) tests + docs + sample snippet for sync and async.
liam: ping me for review. thanks for catching this — could have been bad in production. :thumbsup:
